structure: Part 10, Upload documents. Read in full at commit 04a073b (the checkout's HEAD): app/views/design-release-2.1/upload-documents.html (253 lines: phase banner and back link, notification-status partial, caption and heading, intro copy, a bulleted list of other documents, a details component with a consignment/documents-needed table and a GOV.UK link, then one form holding the error summary, a 'File upload' card with four fields (document reference input, document type select, date of issue MOJ date picker, attachment file drop zone with a requirements list), a 'Save and add another' button, the uploaded-documents table with status tags and Remove buttons, and the shared journey-form-actions partial); app/routes.js 10871-11104 (document type option lookup and labels, select items, uploaded documents list and display statuses, body parsing, validateUploadDocument, add, mark virus check passed, remove, form-state reset, trySavePendingUploadDocument, return query, renderUploadDocumentsPage); app/routes.js 12182-12285 (GET /upload-documents, POST /upload-documents/virus-check/:documentId, POST /upload-documents with remove, add-another, hub/review soft save, continue and fallback branches). To claim every document type and the file limit, also read app/routes.js 10840-10870 (the option constants, MAX_UPLOADED_DOCUMENTS and VIRUS_CHECK_DELAY_MS, which sit just before this part's range), and to say where each action leads, read the helpers it calls: app/routes.js 1500-1602 (journey steps around /upload-documents, getNextJourneyPath, isJourneySoftSaveAction, getJourneySaveRedirect, getSectionContinueRedirect) and 8949-8951 (isDesignRelease21TemplateCreate), plus app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html for the bottom buttons. Those are claimed only as they bear on this page; their own parts own them. The client-side virus-check script in app/assets/ is out of scope and was not read. Covered: the page's route, back link, caption, heading, all copy, every field with its label, hint and options (13 document types), the uploaded-documents table with its two statuses and the Remove action, all five validation messages, the virus-check endpoint, and where remove, add-another, save and return to overview, save and return, save and continue and the fallback each lead. Stops at review.

claims.statement: The upload documents page is served at /upload-documents; under Design Release 2.1 it is reached at /design-release-2.1/upload-documents because the version mount copies every root route under that prefix.
claims.note: The /design-release-2.1 prefix comes from app/lib/version-mount.js, which another part reads.

claims.statement: In the linear journey the upload documents page comes after the transporter page and before roles and addresses.
When the user is creating a template in Design Release 2.1, the upload documents page is left out of the journey steps.
Opening the upload documents page while creating a template in Design Release 2.1 redirects to the notification hub instead of showing the page.
Submitting the upload documents form while creating a template in Design Release 2.1 redirects to the notification hub without saving anything.
Opening the upload documents page ensures the notification has a reference, and the page shows the notification reference, falling back to the prototype's default reference.
Opening the upload documents page clears any earlier errors and any half-entered document reference, type, date of issue and attachment, so the form always opens empty.

claims.statement: The page shows the Alpha phase banner with a feedback-by-email link.
The page has a Back link.
The Back link goes to the review page when the user came from review or is amending the notification, and otherwise to the notification hub.
The page shows the notification status block above the heading.
claims.note: The notification-status partial's own content is claimed by the shell part.

claims.statement: The page caption is 'Documents'.
The page heading is 'Upload documents', which is also the page name.
The intro tells the user they must attach an ITAHC if the consignment requires one and can add it later if they do not have it now.
claims.quote: You must attach an ITAHC if this consignment requires one. If you do not have it now, you can add it later.

claims.statement: The intro tells the user all documents should be uploaded before the consignment arrives at the UK port.
claims.quote: All documents should be uploaded before the consignment arrives at the UK port.

claims.statement: The intro tells the user documents must be in English and every page must be uploaded.
claims.quote: Documents must be in English and you must upload all pages.

claims.statement: The page lists other documents the user may need to attach: import licences or authorisations, and commercial documents or invoices.
claims.quote:
Other documents you may need to attach include:

  • import licences or authorisations
  • commercial documents or invoices

claims.statement: The form posts to /upload-documents under the journey's base path, adding ?from=review or ?from=hub and a matching hidden 'from' field when the user came from review or the hub.

claims.note: The page has no conditional 'other' text field and the validation has no rule for one; looked in the view and validateUploadDocument.

claims.statement: The date of issue field is a Ministry of Justice date picker component, not the GOV.UK three-box date input.
The date of issue has no rule about being in the past or relative to the arrival date; it only has to be a real date.
claims.note: validateUploadDocument checks only presence and parseArrivalDisplayDate; no future-date or range rule exists.

claims.statement: The fourth field is labelled 'Attachment' with the hint 'Your file must be:'.
claims.quote:
...
Your file must be:

claims.statement: The attachment hint says files must be smaller than 50MB.
The attachment hint says the allowed file types are PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX.
claims.quote: • PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX

claims.statement: The attachment hint says up to a maximum of 15 files can be uploaded.
The attachment hint says ZIP files are not allowed for security reasons.
claims.quote: • ZIP files are not allowed for security reasons

claims.statement: The prototype does not enforce the 50MB size limit, the allowed file types or the ZIP ban on the server: no validation checks them.
claims.note: validateUploadDocument checks only the file count, reference, type, date and that a file name is present. No error message exists for a too-large file, a wrong type or a ZIP.

claims.statement: The attachment is a drop zone showing the chosen file name, or 'No file chosen', with a 'Choose file' control and the text 'or drop file'.
claims.quote:
aria-live="polite">{{ formValues.attachmentFileName or "No file chosen" }}
or drop file

claims.statement: The file status line in the drop zone is announced to screen readers as it changes.
The prototype does not upload the file itself: the server records only the chosen file name, sent in a hidden attachmentFileName field.
claims.note: The form has no multipart encoding and the handlers read only body.attachmentFileName; the drop-zone script that fills the hidden field is client-side and out of scope.

claims.statement: On a validation error the page keeps what the user typed in document reference, document type, date of issue and the attachment file name.
Each field shows its own error message beside it, and the attachment field and drop zone take an error style when the attachment is in error.
A 'Save and add another' button below the fields saves the document entered and returns to the same page.
claims.quote:
text: "Save and add another",
            name: "action",
            value: "add-another",

claims.statement: Saving and adding another keeps the ?from=review or ?from=hub return context; amending a notification always counts as coming from review.
Save and add another validates every field; when all pass, the document is added to the list and the form is cleared.
A blank document reference shows the error 'Enter a document reference', linked to the reference field. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed first.
No document type, or a value not in the list, shows the error 'Select a document type', linked to the type field.
claims.quote:
if (!values.documentType || !getDocumentTypeValues(sessionData).includes(values.documentType)) {
    errors.documentType = { text: 'Select a document type' }

claims.statement: A blank date of issue shows the error 'Enter a date of issue', linked to the date field.
claims.quote: errors.dateOfIssue = { text: 'Enter a date of issue' }

claims.statement: A date of issue that cannot be read as a real date shows the error 'Enter a real date', linked to the date field.
claims.quote:
} else if (!parseArrivalDisplayDate(values.dateOfIssue)) {
    errors.dateOfIssue = { text: 'Enter a real date' }
claims.note: The date is parsed with the same parser as the arrival date picker (parseArrivalDisplayDate), which another part reads.

claims.statement: No chosen file shows the error 'Upload a document', linked to the attachment field.
Errors for the reference, type, date and attachment are reported together, in that order, in the error summary.
claims.note: Each check pushes to errorList in sequence without returning early, so all failures show at once.

claims.statement: A notification can hold at most 15 documents.
Saving a document when 15 are already listed shows only the error 'You can upload a maximum of 15 files', linked to the attachment field, and checks nothing else.
claims.quote:
if (uploadedCount >= MAX_UPLOADED_DOCUMENTS) {
    errors.attachment = { text: `You can upload a maximum of ${MAX_UPLOADED_DOCUMENTS} files` }

claims.statement: Each saved document records its reference, type, type label, date of issue, file name, a virus status of 'uploading' and when it was added.
claims.quote:
documentReference: values.documentReference,
    documentType: values.documentType,
    documentTypeLabel: getDocumentTypeLabel(values.documentType, sessionData),
    dateOfIssue: values.dateOfIssue,
    fileName: values.attachmentFileName,
    virusStatus: 'uploading',
    addedAt: Date.now()

claims.statement: Saved documents are kept in the notification's session data as a list of uploaded documents.
The date of issue is stored as the text the user entered, not as a normalised date.
claims.note: parseArrivalDisplayDate is used only to validate; the trimmed raw string is saved and shown in the table.

claims.statement: When at least one document is saved, a table lists them below the 'Save and add another' button with the columns Document reference, Document type, Date of issue, Status and a visually hidden 'Action' column.
claims.quote:
<th scope="col" class="govuk-table__header">Document reference</th>
                    <th scope="col" class="govuk-table__header">Document type</th>
                    <th scope="col" class="govuk-table__header">Date of issue</th>
                    <th scope="col" class="govuk-table__header">Status</th>

claims.statement: With no saved documents, no table is shown.
Each row shows the document reference, the document type's display label and the date of issue as entered.
claims.quote: {{ document.documentReference }} {{ document.documentTypeLabel }} {{ document.dateOfIssue }}

claims.statement: A document of type itahc is labelled 'Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC)' and one of type health-certificate is labelled 'Health certificate'; an unknown type shows its raw value.
A newly saved document's status shows as a blue 'Scanning for virus' tag.
claims.quote:
text: document.virusStatus === 'passed' ? 'Check completed' : 'Scanning for virus',
      class: document.virusStatus === 'passed' ? 'govuk-tag--green' : 'govuk-tag--blue'

claims.statement: Once its virus check has passed, a document's status shows as a green 'Check completed' tag.
The status cell carries visually hidden text 'Virus check status for' followed by the document reference.
The virus check has only two outcomes, scanning and passed; there is no failed or infected status and no message for a file that fails the check.
claims.note: Statuses are 'uploading' and 'passed' only; looked in getUploadedDocumentsForDisplay and markUploadedDocumentVirusCheckPassed.

claims.statement: A POST to /upload-documents/virus-check/{documentId} marks that document's virus check as passed if it is still scanning, and answers with JSON giving its virus status, or null if no such document exists.

The virus check is simulated: the page asks the server to mark each scanning document as passed after a 2.5 second delay, so the tag changes from 'Scanning for virus' to 'Check completed' without a real scan.
claims.note: The server constant is unused in routes.js; the status tag carries data-virus-status and data-document-id for a client script (app/assets/javascripts/upload-documents-virus-check.js, out of scope, not read) that calls the virus-check endpoint. The rendered traces cover the client behaviour.

claims.statement: Each row has a 'Remove' link-styled button.
Remove deletes that document straight away, with no confirmation page, clears the form and reloads the upload documents page keeping the review or hub return context.
Removing a document discards anything typed in the form fields at the time.
claims.note: Remove is a submit inside the same form, but the handler redirects without saving the pending values.

claims.statement: Removing a document that no longer exists does nothing and still reloads the page.
The page ends with the shared journey buttons: by default 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link.
claims.note: The partial's amend and template-review variants are claimed by the shell part; this page passes no options.

claims.statement: Uploading documents is optional: Save and continue with the document type left blank moves on without any error.
claims.quote:
// Soft validation: uploads are optional, but once a document type is chosen
    // all document fields must be completed before continuing.

claims.statement: If a valid document type is chosen when the user presses Save and continue, every document field is validated and, if all pass, the document is saved before moving on.
A reference, date or file entered with no document type chosen is silently discarded on Save and continue or Save and return to overview.
claims.note: Validation only runs once a type is chosen; without one the handler resets the form and redirects.

claims.statement: Save and continue goes to the next journey step, roles and addresses, unless the user came from the hub (back to the hub), from review (back to review) or from a template review (save and return to that template).
Save and return to overview, and Save and return when amending, apply the same optional-upload validation, save the draft notification, and go to the hub or review respectively.
Any other submission clears the form and goes to the notification hub.
On this page only Save and return to overview and Save and return (amend) explicitly save the draft notification; Save and add another, Remove and Save and continue do not call the draft save.
claims.note: persistDraftNotification is called in getJourneySaveRedirect, used only by the hub/review branch; the add-another and remove branches redirect without it. Whether continue persists depends on getSectionContinueRedirect, which does not call it.
